name: a backdated reading inserted between two existing measurements never supersedes
description: Three weight measurements for Wei: note A at 2026-04-01, note B at 2026-04-15, then note C captured last (2026-04-20) but backdated to a DISTINCT instant 2026-04-08 between them. Measurements accumulate and NEVER auto-supersede (docs/reference/ANALYSIS.md fact kinds: measurement = time-series). decide() for kind='measurement' with a distinct valid_from hits the time-series branch (return Decision(insert=True)) — no same-instant clash, so no fact_conflict, no superseded chain. All three stay active regardless of capture order. Pins that out-of-order arrival in a measurement series is harmless: insertion order doesn't matter, only the (metric, instant) identity, and distinct instants coexist.
xfail: TWO accepted gaps. (1) ACCEPTED, on measurement. assert_fact has no `kind` field, and none of this scenario's predicates is declared in the tier-1 registry, so `_fact_kind` falls back to the subject type's default (`attribute` for a Person). An attribute holds a second value for review, so what was a measurement time-series or a clean state supersession is now an attribute_collision. A `kind` field was probed against the live model (evals/shape_probe.py, `fields` suite, gpt-oss-120b, 12 samples an arm): described with its six words in an imperative 'copy exactly ONE of these six words, and never any other word', it came back legal 7 times in 80 - the model writes the fact's TOPIC (`residence` x15, `employment` x10, `medical` x9, `weight` x5) - and 12 in 85 on the full eleven-field surface. Required buys presence, not membership. The route that does work is the one `_fact_kind` already reads: DECLARE the predicate in `src/jbrain/schema/defs/`, where a declared `kind` wins over the subject type's default. That is registry work under ENTITY_GRAPH_REFOCUS_PLAN's tier-1, not tool work. The one enum-free shape that CAN carry a closed vocabulary was tried too and fails the other way round: a `reading` BOOLEAN (is this a number off an instrument?) came back legal 96 times in 96 and `true` 88 of them - on 'Dana still works at Everlane' and 'I finally sold the Civic' alike - so wiring it would make nearly every fact a measurement, which accumulates and never supersedes. The mirror image of the `negated` boolean, which never fires at all. W5 MUST NOT DELETE: `_fact_kind`, the registry's per-predicate `kind` declaration, or the `attribute_collision` card - it is the only thing standing between an undeclared measurement and a silent overwrite. (2) The UNIT is dropped: {kg: 80.0} renders down to the bare number 80.0, because assert_fact's `object` is a string and the harness will not re-spell a value to suit the engine's dedup (runner._object_literal). Two spellings of one weight are therefore incomparable through this surface. ACCEPTED as designed, not open. `assert_fact.object` is a plain STRING and there is no structured `value_json` field: TOOL_SURFACE gap 5's deliberate narrowing, the model is never asked to nest. So a literal is stored as {value} or {value, unit} and anything richer is flattened by runner._object_literal first, while an edge with an object entity stores no value_json at all. W5 MUST NOT DELETE: `facts.value_json`, `_quantity_value`'s unit split, or `supersession.values_equal`'s cross-unit comparison - the EMR importer and the projections write and read structured values through the non-model path.

steps.body: Forgot to log it: on the 8th my weight was 79.6 kg.
